correlates.name: Acute bacterial prostatitis
correlates.presentation: A 63-year-old man has 2 days of fever, frequency, burning on urination, trouble starting his stream and aching in the perineum and low back. T 101.3 F, other vitals stable. Rectal exam: a tense, boggy, exquisitely tender gland; pus appears at the meatus.
correlates.workup: Urine: more than 10 WBC per high-power field; the voided urine culture is positive, most often for a gram-negative enteric rod.
correlates.management: A fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin or norfloxacin) for 2-4 weeks; TMP-SMX only once sensitivities are known. The trap is treating it as a bladder infection for 3-7 days - if symptoms persist, go back and examine the gland.

correlates.name: Chronic bacterial prostatitis
correlates.presentation: A 48-year-old man has had 5 months of on-and-off aching in the perineum and pelvis with mild burning and frequency; two 1-week antibiotic courses helped only briefly. Afebrile, vitals normal. Rectal exam: gland mildly tender, not boggy; no urethral discharge.
correlates.workup: Urine more than 10 WBC per high-power field, yet the voided culture grows few or no bacteria (about 70% are 'sterile'); expressed prostatic secretions can grow the organism.
correlates.management: Still culture the urine and treat empirically at first; if there is pyuria without bacteria, test for chlamydia.

correlates.name: Catheter-associated UTI
correlates.presentation: A 71-year-old man has had an indwelling Foley since hip surgery 9 days ago. Today he has T 38.6 C, new confusion and lower abdominal discomfort; the drainage bag holds cloudy, foul-smelling urine. He reports no burning. HR 104, BP 122/70.
correlates.workup: Urine from the Foley sampling port: pyuria and more than 100,000 CFU/mL of an oxidase-positive, non-lactose-fermenting gram-negative rod; the tubing lumen is crusted and narrowed by biofilm.

correlates.name: UTI in a nursing-home resident
correlates.presentation: An 86-year-old woman in a long-term care facility, incontinent and left in soiled briefs for hours, has 2 days of new confusion, poor appetite, feeling cold and shaking chills. She does not mention burning. T 35.8 C, HR 108, BP 104/60. No Foley.
correlates.management: Send a urine culture with sensitivities before choosing, then use the narrowest drug that covers the isolate: resistant E. coli, Pseudomonas, enterococci, staph and Candida are common in this setting, and broad agents breed C. difficile.
